# dlaln2

> Solves a 1-by-1 or 2-by-2 linear system of equations of the specified form.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaln2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaln2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaln2(
    order,
    ltrans,
    na, nw,
    smin, ca,
    A, LDA,
    d1, d2,
    B, LDB,
    wr, wi,
    X, LDX,
    scale,
    xnorm
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `ltrans` | `boolean` | in |  |  | =`true`: A-transpose will be used. =`false`: A will be used (not transposed.) |
| `na` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | the size of the matrix A. |
| `nw` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | 1 if "w" is real, 2 if "w" is complex. |
| `smin` | `number` | in |  |  | the desired lower bound on the singular values of A. |
| `ca` | `number` | in |  |  | the coefficient c, which A is multiplied by. |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `na × na` |  | the NA x NA matrix A. |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `d1` | `number` | in |  |  | the 1,1 element in the diagonal matrix D. |
| `d2` | `number` | in |  |  | the 2,2 element in the diagonal matrix D. |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `na × nw` |  | the NA x NW matrix B (right-hand side). |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `B` |
| `wr` | `number` | in |  |  | the real part of the scalar "w". |
| `wi` | `number` | in |  |  | the imaginary part of the scalar "w". |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | out | `na × nw` |  | the NA x NW matrix X (unknowns), as computed by DLALN2. |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `X` |
| `scale` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the scale factor that B must be multiplied by to insure that overflow does not occur when computing X |
| `xnorm` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the infinity-norm of X, when X is regarded as an NA x NW real matrix |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ltrans`: =.TRUE.: A-transpose will be used. =.FALSE.: A will be used (not transposed.)
- `na`: The size of the matrix A. It may (only) be 1 or 2.
- `nw`: 1 if "w" is real, 2 if "w" is complex. It may only be 1 or 2.
- `smin`: The desired lower bound on the singular values of A. This should be a safe distance away from underflow or overflow, say, between (underflow/machine precision) and (machine precision \* overflow ). (See BIGNUM and ULP.)
- `ca`: The coefficient c, which A is multiplied by.
- `A`: The `NA` x `NA` matrix A.
- `d1`: The 1,1 element in the diagonal matrix D.
- `d2`: The 2,2 element in the diagonal matrix D. Not used if `NA=1`.
- `B`: The `NA` x `NW` matrix B (right-hand side). If `NW=2` ("w" is complex), column 1 contains the real part of B and column 2 contains the imaginary part.
- `wr`: The real part of the scalar "w".
- `wi`: The imaginary part of the scalar "w". Not used if `NW=1`.
- `X`: The `NA` x `NW` matrix X (unknowns), as computed by DLALN2. If `NW=2` ("w" is complex), on exit, column 1 will contain the real part of X and column 2 will contain the imaginary part.
- `scale`: The scale factor that B must be multiplied by to insure that overflow does not occur when computing X. Thus, (ca A - w D) X will be $\mathrm{SCALE} \, B$, not B (ignoring perturbations of A.) It will be at most 1.
- `xnorm`: The infinity-norm of X, when X is regarded as an `NA` x `NW` real matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaln2.ndarray(
    ltrans,
    na, nw,
    smin, ca,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    d1, d2,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    wr, wi,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    scale,
    xnorm
) → integer
```

Solves a 1-by-1 or 2-by-2 linear system of equations of the specified form, using alternative indexing semantics.

  (ca_A    - w_D) _ X = scale _ B  (if ltrans = false)
  (ca_A__T - w_D) _ X = scale _ B  (if ltrans = true)

where A is NA-by-NA (NA = 1 or 2), w = (wr, wi), D is an NA-by-NA
diagonal matrix, and scale is chosen (0 < scale <= 1) to prevent overflow.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ltrans` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, solve transposed system |
| `na` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of A (1 or 2) |
| `nw` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | 1 for real, 2 for complex system |
| `smin` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound on singular values; clamped to machine threshold |
| `ca` | `number` | in |  |  | scalar multiplier for A |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in | `na × na` |  | matrix A |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | second dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for A |
| `d1` | `number` | in |  |  | D(1,1) diagonal element |
| `d2` | `number` | in |  |  | D(2,2) diagonal element |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `na × nw` |  | right-hand side matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | second dimension stride of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B |
| `wr` | `number` | in |  |  | real part of the scalar w |
| `wi` | `number` | in |  |  | imaginary part of the scalar w |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | out | `na × nw` |  | output matrix (solution) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | first dimension stride of X |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | second dimension stride of X |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for X |
| `scale` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the scale factor that B must be multiplied by to insure that overflow does not occur when computing X |
| `xnorm` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the infinity-norm of X, when X is regarded as an NA x NW real matrix |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ltrans`: =.TRUE.: A-transpose will be used. =.FALSE.: A will be used (not transposed.)
- `na`: The size of the matrix A. It may (only) be 1 or 2.
- `nw`: 1 if "w" is real, 2 if "w" is complex. It may only be 1 or 2.
- `smin`: The desired lower bound on the singular values of A. This should be a safe distance away from underflow or overflow, say, between (underflow/machine precision) and (machine precision \* overflow ). (See BIGNUM and ULP.)
- `ca`: The coefficient c, which A is multiplied by.
- `A`: The `NA` x `NA` matrix A.
- `d1`: The 1,1 element in the diagonal matrix D.
- `d2`: The 2,2 element in the diagonal matrix D. Not used if `NA=1`.
- `B`: The `NA` x `NW` matrix B (right-hand side). If `NW=2` ("w" is complex), column 1 contains the real part of B and column 2 contains the imaginary part.
- `wr`: The real part of the scalar "w".
- `wi`: The imaginary part of the scalar "w". Not used if `NW=1`.
- `X`: The `NA` x `NW` matrix X (unknowns), as computed by DLALN2. If `NW=2` ("w" is complex), on exit, column 1 will contain the real part of X and column 2 will contain the imaginary part.
- `scale`: The scale factor that B must be multiplied by to insure that overflow does not occur when computing X. Thus, (ca A - w D) X will be $\mathrm{SCALE} \, B$, not B (ignoring perturbations of A.) It will be at most 1.
- `xnorm`: The infinity-norm of X, when X is regarded as an `NA` x `NW` real matrix.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

An error flag. It will be set to zero if no error occurs, a negative number if an argument is in error, or a positive number if ca A - w D had to be perturbed. The possible values are:

-   `= 0`: No error occurred, and (ca A - w D) did not have to be perturbed.
-   `= 1`: (ca A - w D) had to be perturbed to make its smallest (or only) singular value greater than `SMIN`. NOTE: In the interests of speed, this routine does not check the inputs for errors.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaln2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaln2';

const scale = new Float64Array( 1 );
const xnorm = new Float64Array( 1 );

// Solve ( ca*A - w*D ) * X = scale*B for a 2x2 system with real w (column-major):
const A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 2.0 ] );
const X = new Float64Array( 2 );
const smin = 1.0e-8;
const ca = 1.0;
const d1 = 1.0;
const d2 = 1.0;
const wr = 0.5;
const wi = 0.0;

// Using the standard interface:
let out = {
	'info': dlaln2( 'column-major', false, 2, 1, smin, ca, A, 2, d1, d2, B, 2, wr, wi, X, 2, scale, xnorm ),
	'scale': scale[ 0 ],
	'xnorm': xnorm[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );
console.log( X );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = {
	'info': dlaln2.ndarray( false, 2, 1, smin, ca, A, 1, 2, 0, d1, d2, B, 1, 2, 0, wr, wi, X, 1, 2, 0, scale, xnorm ),
	'scale': scale[ 0 ],
	'xnorm': xnorm[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );
console.log( X );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLALN2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLALN2 solves a system of the form (ca A - w D ) $X = s$ B or $(\mathrm{ca} A^T - w D)$ $X = s$ B with possible scaling ("s") and perturbation of A. ($A^T$ means A-transpose.)

A is an `NA` x `NA` real matrix, ca is a real scalar, D is an `NA` x `NA` real diagonal matrix, w is a real or complex value, and X and B are `NA` x 1 matrices -- real if w is real, complex if w is complex. `NA` may be 1 or 2.

If w is complex, X and B are represented as `NA` x 2 matrices, the first column of each being the real part and the second being the imaginary part.

"s" is a scaling factor (\<= 1), computed by DLALN2, which is so chosen that X can be computed without overflow. X is further scaled if necessary to assure that $\operatorname{norm}(\mathrm{ca} A - w D) \, \operatorname{norm}(X)$ is less than overflow.

If both singular values of (ca A - w D) are less than `SMIN`, `SMIN`\*identity will be used instead of (ca A - w D). If only one singular value is less than `SMIN`, one element of (ca A - w D) will be perturbed enough to make the smallest singular value roughly `SMIN`. If both singular values are at least `SMIN`, (ca A - w D) will not be perturbed. In any case, the perturbation will be at most some small multiple of max( `SMIN`, ulp\*norm(ca A - w D) ). The singular values are computed by infinity-norm approximations, and thus will only be correct to a factor of 2 or so.

Note: all input quantities are assumed to be smaller than overflow by a reasonable factor. (See BIGNUM.)

</section>
